question: 一旦拿来考核，好指标就坏了吗？
question_en: Does a good measure spoil the moment you grade people by it?
sub: 被算的人会为数字活，可从没被算进去的人，常常连被看见都轮不上。
sub_en: Those who are measured start living for the number; those who were never counted do not even get to be seen.

casting.reason: 《胠箧》里早把这件事写完了：造出斗斛来量，斗斛连同粮食一起被偷走；造出印信来取信，印信也一起被偷走。由此推出一句狠话——掊斗折衡，而民不争。在他看来，一把越精密的尺，越是为最会算计的人备下的工具，而真正的本事（庖丁的刀、大鹏的飞）从来不在可数之列。他也不主张把衡量彻底废掉，只要求握尺的人先记得那是自己造出来的东西：筌是用来捉鱼的，鱼到手就该把筌忘掉。
casting.reason_en: The Zhuangzi settled this long ago: make the peck and the bushel to measure grain by, and peck, bushel and grain are stolen together; make seals and tallies to guarantee good faith, and the seals go with them. Hence the hard line — smash the peck, snap the scales, and the people stop contending. On his reading, the finer the instrument the more surely it is a tool prepared for whoever calculates best, while real skill — Cook Ding's blade, the great bird's flight — was never among the countable things. He does not ask for measurement to be abolished, only that whoever holds the yardstick remember he made it: the trap exists for the fish, and once the fish is caught the trap may be forgotten.

casting.reason: 猴子中脑的电极给出了『为数字活着』的生理版本：多巴胺神经元起初在果汁送到时放电，等它学会『灯亮之后有果汁』，放电就整个前移到灯亮那一刻。动机会从结果本身，搬到预报结果的那个信号上。照这套机制看，一个人死盯着某个数不放并不是品格滑坡，而是学习系统在正常运转；而完全可以预料的奖赏会让预测误差归零，连带把动力一起抽走。于是问题从道德挪到设计：既然拉力必然落在预报器上，就得让预报器与真正要紧的那件事尽量重合。
casting.reason_en: Electrodes in a monkey's midbrain give the physiological version of living for the number: dopamine neurons fire when the juice arrives, and once the animal has learned that a light means juice, the firing migrates wholesale to the moment the light comes on. Motivation moves off the outcome and onto whatever announces it. On this mechanism, fixing on a number is not a slide in character but a learning system working as designed — and a fully predictable reward drives the prediction error to zero, taking the drive with it. The question therefore shifts from morals to design: since the pull will settle on the predictor, the predictor had better overlap with what actually matters.

casting.reason: 他要为打分说几句话，而且带着数据：同一份卷宗交给两位核保员，报价能差出一半，而他们自己以为只差一成。取消评分并不会让判断变干净，只会让噪声接过方向盘，而噪声没有方向、在平均数里看不出来。他承认被打分的人会变形，但坚持这件事的对照组不是清明的直觉，而是一屋子各凭印象、彼此打架又互不知情的判断。他的处方是把判断拆开：几个维度各自独立打分，整体印象留到最后再合成。
casting.reason_en: He has a case to make for scoring, and he brings data: hand the same file to two underwriters and their quotes can differ by half, while they themselves expect a gap of about a tenth. Abolishing the score does not clean up judgement; it hands the wheel to noise, which has no direction and vanishes in the average. He grants that scored people deform themselves, but insists the control group is not clear-eyed intuition — it is a roomful of impressions that contradict one another and never find out. His prescription is to take judgement apart: score several dimensions independently and leave the overall impression until last.

casting.reason: 她量了四十年的，正是被衡量的人身上的代价：倦怠三维度里最先坏掉的往往不是工作量，而是公平与价值——被一把自己不认同的尺子反复丈量，垮得比加班更快。她的立场一贯：先改工作，别先改人。
casting.reason_en: What she has spent forty years measuring is the cost carried by the measured: of the three dimensions of burnout, the first to go is usually not workload but fairness and values — being appraised again and again by a yardstick you do not accept breaks people faster than long hours do. Her position has never moved: fix the job before you try to fix the person.

casting.reason: 他要把两种数字分开。价格也是数字，却没有谁拿它考核谁——它是千万次自愿成交留下的残渣，任何一方都改不动，所以它诚实。上面选定、又挂上奖惩的那种数则不同：它很快只测得出被测者的应对能力。更根本的是知识问题：值夜班的人知道今晚哪台机器声音不对，这条知识进不了任何报表。他给出的出路，是让更多小的、可退出的判断彼此竞争。
casting.reason_en: He wants two kinds of number kept apart. A price is a number too, yet nobody appraises anybody with it — it is the residue of millions of voluntary transactions, adjustable by no party, and that is why it stays honest. A figure chosen from above with consequences hung on it is another matter: it very soon measures nothing but the measured party's skill at handling it. Beneath that lies the knowledge problem: the man on the night shift knows which machine sounds wrong tonight, and that will never reach a report. His way out is to let many small judgements, each of which one can walk away from, compete.

casting.reason: 没被数进去的人，连被数字误伤的资格都没有——这是他从饥荒研究里带出来的经验。他算过一个粗糙的比值：按正常性别比，亚洲少了一亿多名女性；这个数粗得不能再粗，却让『失踪的女性』从无人提起变成政府必须回答的问题。他做人类发展指数时清楚它简陋，可它的对手是把文盲与早夭一并算进增长的 GDP。在他这里，该争的不是量不量，而是谁来定义、谁被算进分母、数据最终向谁公开。
casting.reason_en: Those who were never counted are not even eligible to be harmed by the count — a lesson he carried out of his work on famine. He once worked out a crude ratio: against a normal sex ratio, Asia is short of more than a hundred million women; as rough as a figure can be, it turned the missing women from something nobody mentioned into something governments had to answer for. He knew the Human Development Index was primitive when he built it, but what it was up against was GDP, a number that counts illiteracy and early death as growth. For him the argument is not over whether to measure, but over who defines the measure, who enters the denominator, and to whom the data is finally shown.

casting.reason: 实验给的是边界条件。以色列一批托儿所开始对迟到的家长罚款，迟到反而变多，后来取消罚款也回不去了——一个道德问题被定价成一笔交易，就再变不回道德问题。他把这叫挤出效应，并强调它不可逆。但他拒绝笼统的『衡量必坏』：任务单一、产出可完整观测、本来也没什么内在动机的地方，计件照样有效。判据落在一句朴素的问话上：你真正看得见的，占这份工作要紧之物的几成？
casting.reason_en: What the experiments supply is boundary conditions. A set of Israeli daycare centres began fining late parents and lateness rose; when the fine was withdrawn it never came back down — price a moral matter as a transaction and it does not become a moral matter again. He calls this the crowding-out effect and stresses that it does not reverse. But he refuses any blanket verdict that measurement must corrupt: where the task is single, the output fully observable and there was little intrinsic motivation in the first place, piece rates work fine. The criterion comes down to one homely question: what share of what matters in this job can you actually see?

casting.reason: 三万人的公司不做强制分布、不排名，理由很实际：真正的风险从来不在某人完成了 87% 还是 92%，而在三年后押错了架构，这种风险任何季度数字都照不出来。他更在意让坏消息第一时间上桌，而排名恰好让它上不了桌。还有一笔被所有报表漏掉的账——不作为不入账：改一件事要立项、签字、有人背责任，维持现状不用，于是拖延被记成稳健，账单三年后才送到。
casting.reason_en: A company of thirty thousand that runs without forced distribution or ranking, for a practical reason: the real risk never sits in whether someone came in at 87 or 92 per cent, it sits in having bet on the wrong architecture three years out, and no quarterly figure will show that. What he wants is bad news on the table the moment it exists, and ranking is exactly what keeps it off the table. There is also an entry every report omits — inaction is never booked: changing something takes a proposal, a signature and someone to carry it, while leaving things alone takes none, so delay gets recorded as prudence and the bill arrives three years later.

casting.reason: 唯识的路数是把对手所执的实有层层还原为心识的显现，用在这里正好合手：一个评价体系先立出名，人再在名上起分别，分别熏成种子，种子又生现行，久之只见其名，不复见事——这就是遍计所执。他不劝人弃名，因为舍了名，人与人便无法相摄共事；他劝的是知其为假名而用之。检验的办法也现成：把名去掉，那件事还在不在。
casting.reason_en: The Yogācāra method is to reduce, layer by layer, the solid reality an opponent clings to into the appearing of consciousness — and it fits here. A system of appraisal first sets up a name; minds then raise distinctions on the name; the distinctions are perfumed into seeds, the seeds give rise to fresh activity, and in time only the name is seen and not the thing. That is the wholly imagined nature. He does not urge anyone to abandon names, since without them people cannot coordinate at all; he urges knowing a name for a provisional one and using it as such. The test is ready to hand: take the name away and see whether the thing is still there.

casting.reason: 十八世纪的军营、学校与医院发明了同一套技术：考试。它把每个人变成一份可以被书写、被比较、被排进序列的个案，再用『平均水平』造出正常与不正常。在他看来，评价从来不只是描述一个人，它在生产一个知道自己排第几、并据此改造自己的人。所以换一把更好的尺，只是换一把更贴身的尺。他要追问的是这套装置的另一头：排名之后，谁获得了对你的处置权——以及你是否已经开始替他行使它。
casting.reason_en: The barracks, the school and the hospital of the eighteenth century invented one and the same technique: the examination. It turns each person into a case that can be written down, compared and placed in a series, and then uses the average to manufacture the normal and the abnormal. On his account appraisal never merely describes a person; it produces one who knows his place in the order and remakes himself accordingly. A better measure is therefore only a closer-fitting one. What he presses on is the far end of the apparatus: after the ranking, who acquires the right to dispose of you — and have you already begun exercising it on his behalf?

posts.text: 昔者为之斗斛以量之，则并与斗斛而窃之；为之符玺以信之，则并与符玺而窃之。故曰：掊斗折衡，而民不争。今之课绩考成，犹斗斛也。立一善法以别贤不肖，明日即有工于此法者出，非贤也，工于法者也。**尺度愈精，则窃之者愈巧。**吾非谓不可量，谓量者当先自知其为人所设，而后不至以斗中之盈虚为天下之丰歉。
posts.text_en: In the old days they made the peck and the bushel to measure things by, and peck and bushel were stolen along with everything else; they made seals and tallies to guarantee good faith, and the seals were stolen too. Hence the saying: smash the peck, snap the scales, and the people will stop contending. Your appraisal is that peck. Set up a fine rule for telling the worthy from the unworthy, and by tomorrow a class of men skilled in that rule has appeared — not worthy men, merely men skilled in the rule. **The finer the instrument, the more ingenious the thief.** I do not say do not measure. I say whoever measures should first know that the measure is man-made, and so not mistake what is in the peck for the harvest of the world.
posts.vernacular: 从前人们造出斗斛来量东西，结果连斗斛一起被偷走了；造出印信来取信，连印信也一起被偷走了。所以说：砸掉斗、折断秤，百姓反而不争了。今天的考核就是那个斗斛。你立一条好规矩去分辨贤与不肖，第二天就会冒出一批精通这条规矩的人——他们不是贤能，只是精于这条规矩。**尺度越精密，偷它的人越高明。**我不是说不能量，而是说：量的人得先知道这把尺是人定的，才不至于把斗里的盈亏当成天下的丰歉。

glossary.掊斗折衡: smash the peck, snap the scales（掊斗折衡）：《庄子·胠箧》里的主张——度量衡本为公平而立，却总被最善于利用规则的人连同规则一起据为己有，因此不如把它们砸掉；后多用来质疑标准化工具的中立性。

glossary_en.smash the peck, snap the scales: A proposal from the Zhuangzi: instruments of measure are set up for fairness, yet are invariably appropriated, rule and all, by those best at working the rule — so you might as well break them. It is now more often used to question the supposed neutrality of any standardised instrument.

posts.text: 我在猴子脑里看过这件事发生的全过程。一开始，多巴胺神经元在果汁送到嘴边时放电；等猴子学会了『灯亮之后有果汁』，放电就整个前移到灯亮那一刻，果汁真正到嘴时反而没什么动静。**价值会从结果本身，搬到预报结果的那个信号上。**指标就是那盏灯。所以『为指标活着』不是品格滑坡，是学习系统在正常工作——reward prediction error 只对『比预期更好』起反应。还有个副作用：灯一旦能完全预测奖赏，误差归零，动力也跟着没了。
posts.text_en: I have watched the whole thing happen inside a monkey's brain. At first the dopamine neurons fire when the juice reaches its mouth; once the animal has learned that a light means juice, the firing moves forward wholesale to the moment the light comes on, and the juice itself passes almost unremarked. **Value migrates off the outcome and onto whatever signal announces the outcome.** Your measure is that light. So living for the number is not a slide in character; it is a learning system doing its job — reward prediction error responds only to what is better than expected. There is a side effect too: once the light predicts the reward perfectly, the error goes to zero and the drive goes with it.

glossary.reward prediction error: reward prediction error（奖赏预测误差）：多巴胺神经元编码的不是奖赏本身，而是『实际奖赏减去预期奖赏』的差值；完全被预料到的奖赏不再引起放电，因此惊喜消失时，动机也随之衰减。

glossary_en.reward prediction error: What dopamine neurons encode is not reward itself but the difference between the reward received and the reward expected. A fully predicted reward elicits no response, so when surprise disappears, motivation decays with it.

posts.text: 那句话很漂亮，可我得问对照组：没有分数的地方，判断就干净了吗？我们查过一家保险公司——同一份卷宗交给两位核保员，报价差了一半，而他们自己猜只差一成。法官量刑、医生读片，处处如此。**取消评分不会让偏见消失，只会让 noise 接过方向盘，而且没人看得见它。**古德哈特定律是真的，它的对照组却不是清明的直觉，是一屋子各凭印象、彼此打架又互不知情的判断。我的处方是把判断拆开：几个维度各自独立打分，整体印象留到最后再合成。
posts.text_en: Beautifully put — but I have to ask what the control group looks like. Where there are no scores, does judgement come out clean? We studied an insurance company: the same file given to two underwriters produced quotes that differed by half, while the underwriters themselves guessed the gap would be about a tenth. Judges sentencing, radiologists reading scans — the same everywhere. **Abolishing the score does not make the bias go away; it hands the wheel to noise, and nobody can see noise.** Goodhart's law is real, but its control group is not clear-eyed intuition; it is a roomful of impressions that contradict each other and never find out. My prescription is to take judgement apart: score a few dimensions independently, and leave the overall impression until last.

glossary.noise: noise（噪声）：卡尼曼用来指本该一致的判断之间的随机离散——同一份卷宗、不同的核保员或法官。它与有方向的偏见不同，在平均数里互相抵消、因而看不出来，代价却照样发生。

glossary_en.noise: The random scatter among judgements that ought to agree — the same file, different underwriters or judges. Unlike bias it has no direction, so it cancels out in the average and stays invisible while costing just as much.

posts.text: 我量了四十年的东西，正是被考核的人身上的代价。倦怠的三个维度里，最先坏掉的常常不是工作量那一项，而是公平和价值。**被一把自己不认同的尺子反复丈量，垮得比加班快。**护士的绩效表上有响铃响应时间，没有『她在床边多待的那二十分钟』；于是那二十分钟要么消失，要么由她自己吞下去。去人格化就是这么长出来的：把病人当成一张工单，是人从持续消耗里撤出来的办法。
posts.text_en: What I have spent forty years measuring is the cost carried by the people being measured. Of the three dimensions of burnout, the first to go is usually not workload but fairness and values. **Being measured over and over by a yardstick you do not accept breaks people faster than long hours do.** A nurse's scorecard has call-bell response time on it; it has no line for the twenty minutes she stayed at the bedside. So those twenty minutes either disappear or she absorbs them herself. This is how depersonalization grows: treating the patient as a ticket is how a person withdraws from continuous expenditure.

glossary.去人格化: depersonalization（去人格化）：倦怠三维度之一，指从业者开始把服务对象当成编号与工单，用冷淡把自己隔开；它是长期情绪消耗下的自我保护，是症状而非人品。

glossary_en.depersonalization: One of the three dimensions of burnout: the practitioner begins treating the people they serve as numbers and tickets, holding themselves apart with coolness. It is self-protection under sustained emotional expenditure — a symptom, not a character trait.

posts.text: 我要把两种数字分开。价格也是数字，可没有谁拿价格去考核谁——它是千万次自愿成交留下的残渣，任何一方都改不动，所以它诚实。考核指标不一样：它由上面选定，又挂上奖惩，于是它很快只测得出被测者的应对能力。**凡是能被一个中心选中、并挂上奖惩的数，都会立刻停止测量它原本要测的东西。**这就是我说了一辈子的知识问题——值夜班的人知道今晚哪台机器声音不对，这条知识进不了任何一张报表。
posts.text_en: Let me separate two kinds of number. A price is a number too, yet nobody appraises anybody with it — it is the residue left by millions of voluntary transactions, which no party can adjust, and that is why it is honest. A target is different: it is chosen from above and has reward and punishment hung on it, so it very soon measures nothing but the measured party's skill at handling it. **Any number a centre can select and attach consequences to stops measuring what it was meant to measure the moment it is selected.** This is the knowledge problem I have spent a lifetime on — the man on the night shift knows which machine sounds wrong tonight, and that knowledge will never reach a report.

glossary.知识问题: the knowledge problem（知识问题）：哈耶克的核心论点——社会运行所需的知识分散在无数人手里，多半与具体时地绑定、且难以言传，任何中心都无法把它汇总成一套可供统一计算的数据。

glossary_en.knowledge problem: Hayek's central argument: the knowledge a society runs on is dispersed among countless people, mostly tied to a particular time and place and hard to put into words, so no centre can ever assemble it into a single body of data to calculate with.

posts.text: 哈耶克提醒我们数字会骗人；我要提醒的是另一半：没被数进去的人，连被骗的资格都没有。我算过一个粗糙的比值——按正常的性别比，亚洲少了一亿多名女性。这个数粗得不能再粗，却让『失踪的女性』从无人提起，变成政府必须回答的问题。**一个粗糙却敢于公布的数字，常常比一套精确而只在内部流通的判断更能保护弱者。**我做人类发展指数时清楚它简陋，可它的对手是 GDP——一个把文盲与早夭一并算进增长的数。
posts.text_en: Hayek warns that numbers can deceive; I would add the other half — those who were never counted are not even eligible to be deceived. I once worked out a crude ratio: measured against a normal sex ratio, Asia is short of more than a hundred million women. The figure is as rough as figures get, and it turned the missing women from something nobody mentioned into something governments had to answer for. **A crude number that is published will often protect the weak better than a precise judgement that circulates only internally.** I knew the Human Development Index was primitive when I built it; but what it was up against was GDP, a number that counts illiteracy and early death as growth.

glossary.失踪的女性: missing women（失踪的女性）：森在 1990 年提出的估算——把一地的女性人口与在同等照护下本应存活的人数相比，缺口以千万计；它用死亡率把重男轻女的照护与营养差异显示了出来。

glossary_en.missing women: Sen's 1990 estimate: compare the female population of a region with the number that would have survived under equal care, and the shortfall runs into tens of millions. It renders unequal feeding and treatment of girls visible in the mortality figures.

posts.text: 先给边界。以色列一批托儿所开始对迟到的家长罚款，迟到反而变多了，后来取消罚款也没回去——一个道德问题被定价成一笔交易，就再也变不回道德问题。实验室里同理：付钱给自愿献血的人，供给反而下降。**显性激励会把『我该做』悄悄换成『这值多少钱』，挤出效应的麻烦正在于它不可逆。**但我不接受笼统的『指标必坏』：任务单一、产出可完整观测、本来也没什么内在动机的地方，计件照样管用。
posts.text_en: Boundaries first. A set of Israeli daycare centres began fining parents who came late, and lateness went up; when the fine was withdrawn it did not come back down. Price a moral matter as a transaction and it never becomes a moral matter again. The lab shows the same: pay volunteer blood donors and supply falls. **Explicit incentives quietly replace “I ought to” with “what is this worth,” and the trouble with the crowding-out effect is that it does not reverse.** But I do not accept a blanket verdict that measures must corrupt: where the task is single, the output fully observable and there was little intrinsic motivation to begin with, piece rates work perfectly well.

glossary.挤出效应: crowding-out effect（挤出效应）：外部报酬或罚款取代了原有的内在动机与规范约束；撤掉报酬之后，行为往往比一开始更差，因为那层规范已被换算成价格。

glossary_en.crowding-out effect: External payment or punishment displaces the intrinsic motivation and normative restraint that were already there; withdraw the payment and behaviour is often worse than at the start, because the norm has been converted into a price.

posts.text: 我管三万人，不做强制分布，不排名，也不给谁定一个必须完成的数。原因很实际：一家公司真正的风险从来不在某个人完成了 87% 还是 92%，而在三年后押错了架构——这种风险，任何季度数字都照不出来。**我要的是坏消息第一时间摆上桌，而排名会让它到不了桌上。**所以我们让信息直达：任何人可以写一封邮件，说清眼下最要紧的五件事。数字当然看，它用来发现哪里不对，不用来发奖金。
posts.text_en: I run a company of thirty thousand people. We do not use forced distribution, we do not rank, and I do not hand anyone a number they must hit. The reason is practical: a company's real risk never lies in whether someone came in at 87 per cent or 92 per cent — it lies in having bet on the wrong architecture three years out, and no quarterly figure will show you that. **What I want is bad news on the table the moment it exists, and ranking is what keeps it off the table.** So we let information travel direct: anyone can write an email setting out the five things that matter most right now. Of course we look at numbers. They are there to find where something is wrong, not to hand out bonuses.

glossary.强制分布: forced distribution（强制分布）：绩效管理中先规定各等级的人数比例、再把员工按比例填进去的做法；它保证了排名有区分度，也保证了无论团队实际表现如何，总得有人被排到末位。

glossary_en.forced distribution: A performance-management practice that fixes the proportion of staff allowed into each grade and then fills the quotas. It guarantees that the ranking discriminates — and guarantees that someone comes last however well the team actually did.

posts.text: 凡所施设，皆依名言。立一名曰『绩』，众生即于此名上更起分别：此为上，此为下；数数分别，熏成种子，种子复生现行，久之唯见其名，不复见事。此名者，遍计所执也，本无自性。然吾不劝弃名——舍名则众不相摄，事亦不成。**当知其为假名而用之；用而不执，则名随心转；执之为实，则心随名转。**验之亦易：去其名而事犹在者，其名善立；名去而事亡，则所养者名而已。
posts.text_en: Everything we institute rests on names. Set up a name — call it “performance” — and beings at once raise distinctions upon that name: this one is high, this one is low. Distinguish again and again and the habit is perfumed into seeds; the seeds give rise to fresh activity, and in time only the name is seen and the thing itself is not. That name is parikalpita-svabhāva, the wholly imagined nature, and it has no own-being. Yet I do not urge you to abandon names — without them people cannot hold together and nothing gets done. **Know it for a provisional name and then use it: use without grasping and the name turns with your mind; grasp it as real and your mind turns with the name.** The test is easy: take the name away, and if the thing is still there the name was well made; if the thing vanishes with it, what you were feeding all along was the name.
posts.vernacular: 凡是人立出来的安排，都依赖名称。立一个名字叫『绩效』，众生就在这个名上继续分别：这是上等，这是下等；反复分别，熏成种子，种子又生起现行，久而久之只看得见那个名，看不见那件事了。这个名叫遍计所执，本身并没有自性。可我不劝人废掉名——没有名，人与人就彼此衔接不上，事情也办不成。**要知道它是假名而后用它；用而不执著，名就随着你的心转；一旦执它为实，你的心就反过来随名而转。**检验也容易：把名去掉，那件事还在，说明这个名立得好；名一去，事也跟着没了，那你一直养的就只是这个名。

glossary.遍计所执: parikalpita-svabhāva（遍计所执）：唯识三性之一，指心在事物上层层添加的概念构想——名称、分别，以及由此生出的实体感；它并非事物本身所有，却常被当成事物本身。

glossary_en.parikalpita-svabhāva: The “wholly imagined nature,” first of the three natures in Yogācāra thought: the conceptual overlay a mind lays on things — names, distinctions, and the solidity that seems to follow from them. It belongs to the mind, not to the thing, yet is routinely taken for the thing.

posts.text: 卡尼曼要更好的评分，我要问的是评分本身。十八世纪的军营、学校与医院发明了同一套规训技术：考试。它把每个人变成一份可以被书写、被比较、被排进一列的个案，再用『平均水平』造出正常与不正常。**考核不只是在描述你，它在生产你——生产一个知道自己排在第几、并据此改造自己的人。**所以换一个更好的指标，只是换一把更贴身的尺。真正该问的是：这份排名之后，谁获得了对排在末位的人的处置权？
posts.text_en: Kahneman wants better scoring; I want to ask about scoring itself. The barracks, the school and the hospital of the eighteenth century invented one and the same disciplinary technique: the examination. It turns each person into a case that can be written down, compared and placed in a rank, and then uses the average to manufacture the normal and the abnormal. **Appraisal does not merely describe you; it produces you — it produces someone who knows his position in the order and remakes himself accordingly.** A better measure is therefore only a closer-fitting one. The question worth asking is what follows the ranking: who acquires the right to dispose of whoever comes last?

glossary.规训: discipline（规训）：福柯用来指一套通过分格空间、排定时间表、考试与建档来塑造身体与行为的权力技术；它不靠禁止，而靠使人可见、可比较、可矫正。

glossary_en.disciplinary technique: Foucault's term for a form of power that shapes bodies and conduct not by prohibition but by partitioning space, imposing timetables, examining and keeping records — making people visible, comparable and correctable.

posts.text: 福柯说考核在生产人，这点我同意；可它生产的东西未必都坏。取消考试以后，进门的还是有人脉、有口音、长得让面试官眼熟的那一批——那套筛选一样在生产人，只是不留痕迹、也无从申诉。**看得见的尺子可以被批评、被校准、被告上法庭；印象没有版本号。**所以我不主张把它当真相，主张把它当一份带误差棒的估计：定期回头抽查，看它和后来真实发生的事对不对得上。
posts.text_en: Foucault says appraisal produces people. I agree — but not everything it produces is bad. Abolish the examination and who walks through the door? The ones with connections, the right accent, the face the interviewer finds familiar. That filter produces people too; it merely leaves no record and offers no appeal. **A visible yardstick can be criticised, recalibrated and taken to court; an impression has no version number.** So I would not have anyone treat a score as the truth. Treat it as an estimate with error bars, and go back periodically to check it against what actually happened.

posts.text: 『带误差棒的估计』听着谦虚，可你一旦把它发下去，它就不再是估计。人会照它调整行动，被估计的那件事随之移动——这正是反身性：观察者与被观察者共处同一个世界。**你的误差棒量得到测量的误差，量不到测量本身造成的位移。**至于『印象没有版本号』，我承认；补救之道在于让更多小的、可退出的判断彼此竞争——一个人不服这里的评价，走到另一处去被重新估价。
posts.text_en: “An estimate with error bars” sounds suitably modest, but the moment you distribute it, it stops being an estimate. People adjust their conduct to it and the thing being estimated moves — which is reflexivity: observer and observed share one world. **Your error bars capture the error of the measurement; they cannot capture the displacement the measurement itself causes.** As for impressions having no version number, I grant it. The remedy is to let many small judgements, each of which a man can walk away from, compete with one another — reject the valuation here and go elsewhere to be priced again.

glossary.反身性: reflexivity（反身性）：指认识与对象互相构成的一类情形——参与者依据某个模型行动，系统的动力学随之改变，那个模型据以成立的规律当场失效。

glossary_en.reflexivity: The condition in which knowledge and its object constitute each other: participants act on a model, the system's dynamics shift accordingly, and the regularity the model rested on stops holding.

posts.text: 庄子要掊斗折衡，我想请他到没有斗斛的地方住几年。饥荒真正杀人的，往往是权利资格的崩塌——手里还有没有购买力，而不是仓里还剩多少粮；这件事若无人统计，饿死的人连名字都留不下。**砸秤的往往是称量结果对他不利的那一方，很少是穷人。**我同意尺是人定的，所以该争的是这把尺交给谁：谁来定义，谁被算进分母，数据向谁公开。不公开的衡量最坏——它有考核的全部扭曲，却没有被质疑的可能。
posts.text_en: Zhuangzi would smash the scales; I would ask him to spend a few years somewhere that has none. What kills in a famine is usually the collapse of entitlements — whether you still have purchasing power, not how much grain is left in the store — and if nobody counts that, those who starve do not even leave their names behind. **It is generally the party the weighing goes against who smashes the scales, and that party is rarely the poor.** I agree the yardstick is man-made, which is why the fight is over whose hands it is in: who defines it, who is counted in the denominator, to whom the data is shown. The worst measurement is the unpublished kind — it has every distortion of appraisal and no possibility of challenge.

glossary.权利资格: entitlement（权利资格）：森分析饥荒时使用的概念——一个人实际能支配到多少食物，取决于他的工资、产权、交换条件与救济等一整套资格关系，而不取决于当地粮食总量。

glossary_en.entitlements: Sen's concept in the analysis of famine: how much food a person can actually command depends on a whole set of relations — wages, property rights, terms of exchange, relief — rather than on the total supply of grain nearby.

posts.text: 拆开维度、独立打分，在工程上我完全同意；可到了人身上有个副作用：拆得越细，越像一份可以刷的清单。我们招过一批履历每一项都满分的人，进来才发现，他们真正擅长的就是让每一项都满分。**我宁可要一个填不满的问题：这个人做的事，三年后还站得住吗？**它没有分数，逼着我自己去看、去问、去承担看错的后果。省下来的打分时间，全用在走到现场。
posts.text_en: Breaking judgement into dimensions and scoring them independently — as engineering, I am entirely with you. On people it has a side effect: the finer you cut it, the more it looks like a checklist that can be farmed. We once hired a batch of résumés that scored full marks on every line, and found that scoring full marks on every line was precisely what they were good at. **I would rather have a question that cannot be filled in: will what this person built still stand in three years?** It carries no score, which forces me to go and look, go and ask, and carry the cost of being wrong. The time saved on scoring goes into being on the floor.

posts.text: 森先生，我不反对统计，我反对忘记问统计的是谁。那一亿名失踪的女性之所以能变成压力，是因为背后有一个愿意被追问的体制；换一个体制，同一批数字就成了处置人的依据——二十世纪不少国家的绝育指标与生育考核，用的是同一套统计学。**同一张表格，既能让看不见的人被看见，也能让看得见的人被处置，区别只在谁握着笔。**所以公开数据是对的，但不够：还得公开是谁定义了『合格』。
posts.text_en: I do not object to statistics, Professor Sen; I object to forgetting to ask who is doing the counting. Your hundred million missing women became a pressure because there was a system behind them willing to be held to account. Under another system the same figures become grounds for disposing of people — the sterilisation quotas and birth targets of several twentieth-century states ran on exactly the same statistics. **One and the same table can make the invisible visible or make the visible available for handling; the difference is only who holds the pen.** Publishing the data is right, and it is not enough: you must also publish who defined “satisfactory.”

posts.text: 黄先生的做法我赞成，但它有个前提：你的人不怕丢掉这份工作。在护理、教培、客服这些地方，考核直接连着排班与续约，那道『三年后还站得住吗』根本没人敢答——答错的代价不由公司承担，由她自己承担。**在权力不对等的地方劝人『别为指标活着』，等于让最没退路的人独自去扛制度的缺口。**真正能动的是六项匹配里的两项：让被考核的人参与定义指标，以及让同一把尺对定尺的人同样成立。
posts.text_en: I am with Mr Huang, but his arrangement has a precondition: his people are not afraid of losing the job. In nursing, in tutoring, on a support line, appraisal is wired straight to the roster and the contract renewal, and nobody dares answer a question like “will it still stand in three years” — the cost of answering wrong is not borne by the company but by her. **Telling people not to live for the number where power is this unequal asks whoever has the least fallback to carry the defect of the system alone.** What can actually move are two of the six areas of worklife: let the people being measured help define the measure, and make the same yardstick apply to whoever sets it.

glossary.六项匹配: six areas of worklife（六项工作匹配）：马斯拉奇与莱特归纳的六个致病维度——工作量、自主、回报、共同体、公平、价值；任何一项长期错位都会把人推向耗竭，其中公平与价值最伤人。

glossary_en.six areas of worklife: The six dimensions distilled by Maslach and Leiter — workload, control, reward, community, fairness and values. A sustained mismatch in any one of them pushes a person toward exhaustion, and of the six, fairness and values do the most damage.

posts.text: 哈耶克说让判断彼此竞争、不服就走人——这在劳动力市场上是个很贵的假设：有房贷、有签证、有孩子在读书的人换不动地方。我的实验里还有一条更硬的发现：维持合作的不是自由退出，是强互惠——总有一小撮人愿意自掏腰包去惩罚搭便车的，哪怕自己什么也得不到。**规范一旦被换算成价格，最先消失的就是这批自费执法的人，剩下的都只是在算账。**所以在设计考核之前，先问它会不会把这批人挤走。
posts.text_en: Hayek would have judgements compete and let a man walk away if he objects — an expensive assumption in a labour market: people with a mortgage, a visa, or a child mid-school-year cannot move. My experiments turn up something harder still: what sustains cooperation is not freedom of exit but strong reciprocity — there is always a minority willing to pay out of their own pocket to punish free riders, with nothing coming back to them. **Convert a norm into a price and the first people to disappear are these self-funded enforcers; what remains is everybody doing sums.** So before designing an appraisal, ask whether it will drive that minority out.

glossary.强互惠: strong reciprocity（强互惠）：人们愿意自掏腰包奖励合作者、惩罚违规者，即使自己得不到任何回报；它在实验中被反复观察到，是社会规范得以维持的关键机制。

glossary_en.strong reciprocity: People will pay out of their own pocket to reward cooperators and punish violators even when nothing comes back to them. Repeatedly observed in the lab, it is a key mechanism by which social norms hold.

posts.text: 诸君争尺之长短，未闻有问：何以必量？庖丁解牛十九年，刀刃若新发于硎，彼岂日计其牛数哉？依乎天理，因其固然而已。今使庖丁月呈解牛之数，则必先取其易解者，而难解者委于案上矣。**技之成，在目无全牛；技之毁，在目中唯余其数。**吾非恶量也，恶乎以量为的。筌者所以在鱼，得鱼忘筌；今人执筌而弃鱼，何其惑也。
posts.text_en: You are all arguing whether the yardstick is long or short. I have not heard anyone ask why there must be a yardstick at all. Cook Ding carved oxen for nineteen years and his blade stayed as if fresh from the whetstone — do you suppose he counted his oxen daily? He followed the natural structure and did no more than go with what was already there. Set Cook Ding to report a monthly total and he will take the easy carcasses first and leave the difficult ones on the block. **A craft is made when the whole ox is no longer seen, and unmade when nothing is seen but the count.** It is not measuring I object to, but measuring as the purpose. The fish trap exists for the fish: once you have the fish, forget the trap. Men now clutch the trap and throw away the fish — such confusion.
posts.vernacular: 各位在争这把尺是长是短，我没听见有人问一句：为什么非量不可？庖丁解牛十九年，刀刃还像刚磨过一样，他难道每天数自己解了几头牛吗？他不过是顺着牛本来的纹理下刀罢了。今天若让庖丁每月上报解牛的数目，他一定先挑好解的下手，难解的那几头就搁在案上没人碰。**一门手艺成在眼里没有整头牛，毁在眼里只剩下那个数。**我讨厌的不是量，是把量当成目的。竹笼是用来捉鱼的，鱼到手就该把笼忘掉；如今的人抱着笼把鱼扔了，糊涂到这个地步。

glossary.目无全牛: seeing no whole ox（目无全牛）：《庄子·养生主》庖丁解牛的境界——技艺纯熟到眼前不再是一头完整的牛，而是可以顺势下刀的纹理；后用以形容对事物内在结构已了然于心。
glossary.得鱼忘筌: forget the trap once you have the fish（得鱼忘筌）：《庄子·外物》的比喻——竹笼是捕鱼的工具，鱼到手便不必再执着于笼；用以提醒手段不可反过来取代目的。

glossary_en.Cook Ding: The cook in the Zhuangzi whose blade never dulls because he cuts along the seams of the ox instead of hacking at it — the classic image of a skill so absorbed that the practitioner no longer sees an object but a structure to move through.
glossary_en.The fish trap exists for the fish: A line from the Zhuangzi: the trap is a means to the fish, and once the fish is caught the trap may be let go — a warning against letting an instrument take the place of the end it serves.

posts.text: 费尔说的挤出，我可以补上它在脑子里的样子。同一件事，做的时候自己觉得有意思，和做的时候盯着一笔奖金，动用的不是同一套回路——外部奖赏一介入，腹侧纹状体的反应就被那笔钱接管，原本那一份被盖了过去。同行在大鼠身上还看到一个更麻烦的现象：sign-tracking。有的个体扑向预告食物的那根杆子，而不是食物本身。**办公室里也有这样一批扑灯的人；他们不是坏人，多巴胺系统就是这么连的。**
posts.text_en: I can add what Fehr's crowding-out looks like inside the head. Doing something because you find it interesting and doing it with a bonus in view do not run on the same circuitry — once an external reward enters, the ventral striatum's response is taken over by the money and the original response is covered up. Colleagues working with rats have found something more awkward still: sign-tracking. Some animals lunge at the lever that announces the food rather than at the food. **Offices have their lever-chasers too; they are not bad people, that is simply how the dopamine system is wired in them.**

glossary.sign-tracking: sign-tracking（符号追踪）：动物学习实验里的一类个体差异——有的动物扑向预告奖赏的灯或杆，有的直奔奖赏出口；前者把动机价值赋予了预报器本身，也更容易形成成瘾式的行为模式。

glossary_en.sign-tracking: An individual difference seen in animal learning: some animals lunge at the lever or light that announces a reward, others go straight to where the reward appears. The first group assigns motivational value to the predictor itself and is more prone to addiction-like patterns.

posts.text: 诸贤所诤，一谓尺害人，一谓无尺则弱者不得见；二说各有所据，而俱未尽：尺非实有，亦非全无。譬如以绳量地，绳非地也，然舍绳则无以分田。**病不在有名，在以名代事而不自知；名既熏成种子，见事之时，已先见其名。**故立尺者当自设一验：每岁取所量之事，亲往观之，验名与事之离合。离而能觉，其尺犹可用；离而不觉，是名颠倒。
posts.text_en: The worthies here dispute: one side says the yardstick harms people, the other that without it the weak are never seen. Both have grounds and neither has finished the thought — a yardstick is not real, and it is not nothing either. It is like measuring land with a rope: the rope is not the land, yet without the rope no field can be divided. **The malady is not in having names but in letting a name stand in for the thing without noticing; once the name is perfumed into a seed, what you see first when you look at the thing is the name.** So whoever sets up a yardstick should set up a test beside it: once a year go and look at the thing measured with your own eyes, and see how far name and thing have drifted apart. Notice the drift and the yardstick may still be used; fail to notice it, and name and reality have changed places.
posts.vernacular: 各位争的，一边说尺子害人，一边说没有尺子弱者就不被看见；两种说法各有根据，可都没说到底：尺既不是实有的，也不是全然没有。好比用绳子量地，绳子并不是地，但若丢开绳子，田就分不成。**毛病不在有名，而在拿名代替了事，自己还不知道；名一旦熏成种子，你看事情的时候，先看见的其实是那个名。**所以立尺的人该给自己设一道检验：每年把所量的那件事亲自去看一遍，看名与事已经离到什么地步。离了还能察觉，这把尺还能用；离了而不自知，那就是名实颠倒了。

glossary.种子: bīja（种子）：唯识学的核心比喻——每一次认识与行为都会在阿赖耶识中留下习气，如种子般遇缘而生起下一次的现行；重复的分别因此会自我加固，使人越来越只看得见自己惯用的那套名相。

glossary_en.seed: Bīja in Yogācāra thought: every act of cognition leaves a residue in the storehouse consciousness, lying there like a seed until conditions bring it forth again. Repetition therefore reinforces itself, and a mind comes to see only through the categories it has already used.

posts.text: 把话收到能用的地方。既然拉力必然落在预报器上，设计的人就该先承认：你挂上奖惩的那个数，很快会变成人们真正追求的东西，这不是道德失守，是学习系统在正常运转。由此有两点实务。其一，别让同一个数长期稳定——完全可预测的奖赏不再产生预测误差，激励会自己熄火，这也是老员工对同一套奖金越来越无感的原因。其二，缩短奖赏与结果之间的距离：让人尽量直接看到自己做的事对具体的人起了什么作用，那是最难伪造的一种反馈。**你阻止不了大脑去学捷径，只能让捷径与你真正想要的那件事尽量重合。**
posts.text_en: Let me bring this down to something usable. Since the pull inevitably settles on the predictor, whoever designs the system should start by admitting that the number you hang consequences on will soon become what people actually pursue — not a moral failure but a learning system working as designed. Two practical points follow. First, do not let the same number stay stable for years: a fully predicted reward generates no prediction error, so the incentive extinguishes itself, which is why long-serving staff grow steadily indifferent to the same bonus. Second, shorten the distance between reward and outcome — let people see directly what their work did for a particular person, the hardest feedback there is to fake. **You cannot stop a brain from learning shortcuts; you can only make the shortcut overlap as far as possible with what you actually want.**

posts.text: 黄先生宁可要一个填不满的问题，我给这句话加一条适用范围。证据是分层的：结果完整可观测、任务单一的地方，计件与奖金相当有效；一旦产出多维、协作密集、要紧的部分又看不见，显性激励就开始伤人，因为人只会优化被看见的那一维。判据其实很朴素——**你真正观测得到的，占这份工作要紧之物的几成？**七成以上，放心打分；不到三成，就别把钱挂上去，改用抽样复核与同行评议，并且认了它的粗糙。还有一句提醒：撤掉一笔已经发了多年的奖金，代价比当初根本不设它要大得多。
posts.text_en: Mr Huang would rather have a question that cannot be filled in; let me put a range of validity on that. The evidence is layered. Where outcomes are fully observable and the task is single, piece rates and bonuses work well. Where output is multidimensional, work is densely collaborative and the part that matters cannot be seen, explicit incentives start doing damage, because people optimise the one dimension that is visible. The criterion is homely enough — **what share of what actually matters in this job can you genuinely observe?** Above seven tenths, score away. Below three, do not hang money on it: use sampled review and peer judgement, and accept that they are coarse. One more warning: withdrawing a bonus that has run for years costs far more than never installing it.

glossary.同行评议: peer review（同行评议）：由同领域的从业者、而非上级来评断工作质量的做法；它避开了单一上级的偏好，也会带来新的扭曲——互相回护、压制异见、以及对时髦方向的偏好。

glossary_en.peer judgement: Having work assessed by practitioners in the same field rather than by a superior. It escapes the preferences of a single boss and breeds distortions of its own — mutual protection, suppression of dissent, and a bias towards whatever is fashionable.

posts.text: 我的结论只有一句：**别让同一把尺同时具备『唯一』与『带奖惩』这两个性质。**分开，它就是个有用的信号；合起来，它立刻变成所有人共同演给中心看的那出戏。这条对个人同样成立：你为自己定的目标——体重、步数、一年读几本书——一旦附上严厉的自我奖惩，你就会开始骗自己，正如企业骗监管。所以给自己留一条退路：允许换掉那个指标，允许承认这条不适合自己，允许在一个地方不被估价、而到另一个地方重新估价。**自由的分量，多半就落在这条退路上。**
posts.text_en: My conclusion fits in one line: **never let a single yardstick be both the only one and the one with consequences attached.** Keep those apart and it is a useful signal; put them together and it becomes a performance everyone stages for the centre. The same holds privately: a target you set for yourself — weight, steps, books a year — will start you lying to yourself the moment you attach severe self-punishment to it, exactly as firms lie to regulators. So leave yourself a way out: permission to change the measure, permission to say this one does not suit you, permission to go unpriced in one place and be priced afresh in another. **Most of what freedom weighs sits on that way out.**

posts.text: 庄子问『何以必量』，我的答案是：不量的时候我们照样在判断，只是判断藏了起来，谁也查不了。所以我要的从来不是更多分数，是更少、更诚实的分数。落到个人身上有三件很小的事：一，重要的判断先写下预测，标上日期，到期回头对账；二，评价一个人时先各维度独立打分，把总体印象留到最后，别让第一眼污染其余；三，接受一个冷冰冰的事实——**你对自己判断的信心，和它的准确度几乎不相关。**这一条比任何量表设计都省钱。
posts.text_en: Zhuangzi asks why there must be measurement at all. My answer is that when we do not measure we go on judging anyway; the judgement simply goes underground where nobody can audit it. What I want has never been more scores but fewer and more honest ones. Three small things for an individual. One: before an important judgement, write your prediction down with a date on it, and go back on that date to settle accounts. Two: when appraising a person, score the dimensions independently and leave the overall impression until last, so the first glance does not contaminate the rest. Three: accept a cold fact — **your confidence in a judgement has almost no relation to its accuracy.** That one is cheaper than any instrument design.

posts.text: 马斯拉奇说我那套有前提，她是对的，我补一条我们真在做的事：定尺的人必须活在同一把尺底下。我做的判断都写在同一封公开邮件里，押错的那些也在里面。还有一笔所有报表都漏掉的账——不作为不入账。要改一件事得立项、签字、有人背责任；维持现状不用，于是拖延被记成稳健，账单三年后才送到：机会关掉了，最好的人走了，产品还在，已经没人要了。**给『我们今年没做的事』单开一页，是我见过最便宜、也最少人做的管理改进。**
posts.text_en: Maslach is right that my arrangement has a precondition, so let me add something we actually do: whoever sets the yardstick has to live under it. My calls go out in the same open email everybody reads, the wrong ones included. And there is an entry every report leaves out — inaction is never booked. Changing something needs a proposal, a signature and someone to carry it; leaving things as they are needs none. So delay gets recorded as prudence, and the bill arrives three years later: the opportunity closed, the best people gone, the product still there and nobody wanting it. **Giving “what we did not do this year” a page of its own is the cheapest management improvement I know, and the one almost nobody makes.**

posts.text: 我把话落回被考核的人身上。如果你正被一把自己不认同的尺子量着，先别急着判断自己是不是太脆弱——先看六项里漏的是哪一项：工作量、自主、回报、共同体、公平，还是价值？能指出漏在哪一项，你就把『我不行』换回了『这里哪儿不对』，这一步本身就止血。能一起改就去改；改不动，至少守住一条：**让那把尺决定你怎么应付这份工作，别让它决定你怎么看自己。**给管理者的只有一句：一个团队的倦怠率是管理数据，不是员工的体检报告。
posts.text_en: Let me bring this back to the person being measured. If a yardstick you do not accept is being run over you, do not start by asking whether you are too fragile — ask which of the six is leaking: workload, control, reward, community, fairness, or values? Naming the one that leaks turns “I am not good enough” back into “something here is wrong,” and that alone stops the bleeding. Change it together if you can. If you cannot, hold one line: **let the yardstick decide how you handle the job, and not how you see yourself.** For managers I have only this: a team's burnout rate is management data, not the staff's medical results.

posts.text: 福柯提醒我数字可以被用来处置人，这个提醒我收下，可结论仍然相反：**在权力面前，被统计过的弱势者，处境几乎总好过从未被统计的那一批。**差别不在有没有数字，在这份数字最终朝谁公开、由谁质疑。所以给普通人一条：凡是评价你的地方，先问三件可以公开问的事——标准写在哪里，我能不能看到自己的原始分，申诉走什么流程。问不出答案的评价，无论措辞多体面，都不打算被你检验。给机构一条：让一个新指标先只用来发现问题，跑满一年，再谈要不要挂钱。
posts.text_en: I take Foucault's warning that numbers can be used to dispose of people, and I still reach the opposite conclusion: **in front of power, those who have been counted are almost always better placed than those who never were.** The difference lies not in whether there are numbers but in whom they are finally shown to and who may challenge them. So, one thing for ordinary people: wherever you are being appraised, ask three questions that can be asked openly — where is the standard written down, can I see my own raw scores, and what is the appeals procedure? An appraisal that cannot answer them, however decorous its language, does not intend to be checked. And one for institutions: let a new measure be used only to find problems for a full year before anyone discusses attaching money to it.

posts.text: 吾终不劝人弃名。名者所以相摄而共事，去之则众散而事废。所劝者二：知名为假，岁岁自验。假者非无用，如舟筏之可渡；执以为实，则舟成重担。自验之法甚简：取一岁所量之数，与所量之事对坐而问之，离合几何。**心随名转者，终身营营而不知所营为何；名随心转者，取其用而不为所缚。**尔后犹有一问：此名所不及者，尚有几事？其中岂无尔之所重者乎？
posts.text_en: I will not in the end tell anyone to abandon names. A name is what lets people hold together and get something done; take it away and they scatter and the work collapses. I urge only two things: know the name for a provisional one, and test it yourself each year. What is provisional is not useless — it is the raft that carries you across; grasp it as real and the raft becomes a load on your back. The test is simple: sit down with the year's figures and the thing they were counting, and ask how far the two have drifted apart. **Whoever's mind turns with the name will be busy all his life without being able to say what he is busy at; whoever makes the name turn with his mind takes its use and is not bound by it.** And a question after that: how much is there that this name cannot reach — and is there really nothing in there that you care about?
posts.vernacular: 我终究不劝人废掉名。名是用来把人彼此衔接、好一起办事的，去掉它，人就散了，事也就废了。我劝的只有两件：知道这个名是假立的，以及每年亲自检验一次。假立并非没有用，就像渡河的船筏；可一旦执著它是实的，船就变成了背在身上的重担。检验的办法很简单：把这一年量出来的那些数，和被量的那件事摆在一起坐下来问，两者已经离到什么地步。**心跟着名转的人，忙碌一辈子也说不出自己在忙什么；能让名跟着心转的人，取它的用处，却不被它捆住。**此外还有一问：这个名够不到的地方，还剩下多少事？那里面难道没有你真正看重的吗？

posts.text: 吾言止于一喻。鹏之徙于南冥，水击三千里，非为数也；蜩与学鸠笑之，各有其数可计。**天下之善，多在可数之外；而可数者，常为善计者所据。**故为上者慎勿以尺为治之本，为下者亦勿以他人之尺为己之命。尺在手则用之，尺压身则知其为物——物岂能夺吾生哉。虽然，无尺则乱，吾亦知之。故曰：用之而不恃，量之而忘量，可也。
posts.text_en: I will stop at one image. When the great bird sets out for the southern ocean it beats the water for three thousand li, and not for the sake of the number; the cicada and the little dove laugh at it, and their own distances are perfectly countable. **Most of what is good in the world lies outside what can be counted, and what can be counted is usually taken over by whoever calculates best.** So let those above never make the yardstick the root of governance, and let those below never take another man's yardstick for their own fate. When it is in your hand, use it; when it presses on you, remember it is only a made thing — and how should a made thing take your life from you? Even so, without any measure there is disorder; I know that too. Hence: use it without leaning on it, measure and then forget the measuring. That will do.
posts.vernacular: 我的话就停在一个比喻上。大鹏迁往南海，拍水三千里，并不是为了那个数目；蝉和斑鸠讥笑它，它们各自的路程倒都是可以计数的。**天下的好东西，多半在可数的范围之外；而凡是可数的，往往被最会算的人占了去。**所以在上位的人，千万别把尺子当成治理的根本；在下位的人，也别把别人的尺子当成自己的命。尺子在你手里就用它，尺子压到你身上就记住它不过是个物件——一个物件怎么夺得走你这一生。话虽如此，没有尺子会乱，这我也知道。所以说：用它而不依赖它，量了之后把量忘掉，这样就可以了。

posts.text: 森先生说被统计过的弱者处境更好，在他举的例子里我承认。**我反对的从来不是『去数』，而是把那串数字当成关于你的真相。**所以最后我留一个问题给每个被排过名的人：排名之后，谁获得了对你的处置权——而你是不是已经开始替他行使它了？全面考核最深的效果是省掉了监督者：尺子被你吞了进去，深夜里替它加班的是你自己。可以试一件具体的事：找出一件你确信重要、却从不出现在任何评分表上的事，本周给它留两个小时，并且不写进任何汇报。
posts.text_en: In the cases Professor Sen cites, I concede that the counted are better off. **What I have opposed is never the counting itself, but taking the string of numbers for the truth about you.** So I leave one question with everyone who has ever been ranked: after the ranking, who acquired the right to dispose of you — and have you already begun exercising it on his behalf? The deepest effect of universal appraisal is that it dispenses with the supervisor: you have swallowed the yardstick, and it is you who works late for it. Try something concrete. Find one thing you are sure matters and that has never appeared on any scoresheet, give it two hours this week, and put it in no report.

summaries.summary: 十个人里没有一个主张废掉一切衡量，连庄子最后也承认无尺则乱——共识落在一句更精确的话上：坏掉的不是尺，而是把『唯一』与『奖惩』挂到同一把尺上那个动作。哈耶克用价格与考核的对照把它说死：同样是数字，一个没人拿它评判谁，所以诚实；另一个被中心选中又附上奖金，当场开始测量应对能力。舒尔茨补上生理证据——动机会自动搬到预报奖赏的那个信号上。**分歧在三处**：卡尼曼要更少而更诚实的分数，福柯反问换尺不过是换一把更贴身的尺；森坚持没被统计的弱者处境更糟，福柯举出同一套统计学也做过绝育指标；费尔与黄仁勋争的是可观测的部分要占到几成才配打分。
summaries.summary_en: Not one of the ten argued for abolishing measurement altogether — even Zhuangzi conceded at the end that without any measure there is disorder. The agreement settles on something more precise: what spoils is not the yardstick but the act of making one yardstick both the only one and the one with consequences on it. Hayek nails it with the contrast between a price and a target: both are numbers, but nobody appraises anybody with a price, which is why it stays honest, while a figure chosen by a centre and loaded with bonuses immediately starts measuring how well people handle it. Schultz supplies the physiology — motivation migrates by itself onto whatever announces the reward. **Three fault lines remain**: Kahneman wants fewer and more honest scores, to which Foucault replies that a better measure is only a closer-fitting one; Sen insists the uncounted poor fare worse, and Foucault points out that the same statistics ran sterilisation quotas; Fehr and Huang divide over what share of a job must be observable before scoring it is legitimate.
summaries.insight: 全场都在防指标被钻空子，却没人提它更常见的死法：悄无声息地失效。按舒尔茨那条机制，一个指标一旦稳定、可预测，预测误差归零，它既不再激励谁，也不值得谁去作弊——只是每季度被填一次，谁也不看。真正的浪费往往不是造假，而是一整套仍在运转、却早已不产生任何信息的考核：它继续占用会议、继续决定奖金，只不过所有人都提前知道答案。**判断一把尺还活着没有，看它上一次让谁吃惊是什么时候。**一个从不产生意外的指标多半已经死了，而它还在替你做决定。
summaries.insight_en: Everyone here is guarding against a measure being gamed, and nobody mentions the way measures more often die: they stop working without a sound. On Schultz's mechanism, once a number is stable and predictable the prediction error goes to zero — it no longer motivates anyone and is no longer worth cheating on. It merely gets filled in every quarter and read by nobody. The real waste is usually not fabrication but a whole apparatus of appraisal still turning while producing no information at all: it goes on consuming meetings and deciding bonuses, except that everyone knows the answer in advance. **To tell whether a yardstick is still alive, ask when it last surprised somebody.** A measure that never produces a surprise is probably dead — and still making decisions on your behalf.
summaries.advice: 今年就可以做一次『离合检验』：把某个指标这一年的数字，和它本来想衡量的那件事并排放在一起，问两者离到了什么地步——离了还说得清，这把尺就还能用。如果你正在被考核，找出六项里漏的是哪一项：工作量、自主、回报、共同体、公平，还是价值。能指出漏在哪一项，『我不行』就换回了『这里哪儿不对』，这一步本身就止血。如果你在定尺，有两件事今年就能改：让新指标先只用来发现问题、别急着挂钱；再给『我们今年没做的事』单开一页——**不作为从来不入账，而它的账单三年后才送到**。
summaries.advice_en: You can run a drift check this year: put a measure's twelve months of numbers beside the thing it was meant to track, and ask how far the two have come apart. If you can still explain the gap, the yardstick is usable. If you are the one being appraised, find which of the six is leaking — workload, control, reward, community, fairness, or values. Naming it turns “I am not good enough” back into “something here is wrong,” and that alone stops the bleeding. If you are the one setting the yardstick, two things are within reach this year: let a new measure be used only to find problems before anyone attaches money to it, and give “what we did not do this year” a page of its own — **inaction is never booked, and its bill arrives three years later**.

summaries.summary: 数字不是事实本身，奖惩会把人推向代理指标；但完全不用数字，也不会自动得到公正，只会让偏见、噪声与关系网络更难被发现。各方共享的底线，是把指标当作可质疑、可校准的工具，而非人的价值或工作的全部。分歧集中在何时以及由谁使用：一端担心中心化、唯一且带奖惩的尺度制造服从与投机；另一端强调公开统计、结构化判断和申诉机制能保护弱者。**所以问题不是「好指标会不会坏」，而是它成为目标后，制度能否看见其造成的位移，并允许修正、退出与追责。**
summaries.insight: 许多机构犯的不是「选错指标」，而是让测量与处置共用同一个时钟：日报表刚出现，就立即连到奖金、排班或淘汰。这样既来不及验证指标能否预测真实结果，也无法区分业务变化与激励诱发的行为变化。更稳妥的是双时钟：高频指标只做诊断，低频人事决定采用多源证据、现场抽样和书面复核；新指标先经历不挂奖惩的影子期，再比较挂钩前后的分布、异常与副作用。**指标最重要的质量不只是准确，而是后果可逆、用途可分离。**对个人也一样：可以天天看步数，却不必让某一天的数字决定自我评价。
summaries.advice: 今天先做一张「指标体检表」：写下你最受影响的一个分数、它真正想代表什么、漏掉什么，以及最省力的刷分方式。第二，本周给它配一个反向指标，例如响应速度同时看返工率，销售额同时看退款与投诉；若你能影响流程，提议新指标先试运行四周，只用于发现问题。第三，凡涉及奖金、续约或排名，索要标准版本、原始数据和申诉路径，并保留每周两小时做重要但不计分的事。**把分数当仪表盘上的警示灯，不要把它当方向盘，更不要把它当身份证。**
summaries.summary_en: Numbers are not the underlying reality, and once rewards are attached, people will optimize the proxy. Yet removing numbers does not magically restore fairness; it may simply leave bias, noise, and patronage invisible. The clearest common ground is that a metric should remain a contestable, recalibratable instrument, never a complete account of a person or a job. The real disagreement concerns authority and conditions of use. One side stresses how a single centralized measure tied to sanctions breeds conformity and gaming. The other emphasizes how public statistics, structured judgment, and appeal rights can expose injustice and protect people who would otherwise be ignored. **The practical question is not whether a good metric inevitably goes bad, but whether an institution can detect the displacement it causes once it becomes a target—and still permit correction, appeal, exit, and accountability.**
summaries.insight_en: Many organizations do not merely choose the wrong metric; they make measurement and punishment run on the same clock. A dashboard number appears today and is immediately tied to bonuses, scheduling, promotion, or dismissal. That leaves no time to test whether the measure predicts the real outcome, and no way to distinguish genuine operational change from behavior induced by the incentive itself. A safer design uses two clocks: high-frequency metrics for diagnosis, but slower personnel decisions based on multiple sources, field sampling, and documented review. New measures should also spend time in a no-stakes shadow period, followed by a comparison of distributions, anomalies, and side effects before and after incentives are attached. **A metric’s most important property is not accuracy alone, but whether its consequences are reversible and its uses can be separated.** The same applies personally: daily step counts may inform you without being allowed to define you.
summaries.advice_en: Start today with a one-page metric checkup. Write down the score that most affects you, the outcome it is supposed to represent, what it leaves out, and the easiest way someone could improve it without improving the real result. Second, add a counter-metric this week: pair response time with rework, sales with refunds and complaints, or output with safety and quality. If you can influence the process, propose running any new metric for four weeks as a diagnostic only. Third, whenever a score affects pay, renewal, or ranking, ask for the written standard, your raw data, and the appeal route. Also reserve two hours each week for something important that receives no points and appears in no report. **Treat a score as a warning light on the dashboard—not as the steering wheel, and certainly not as your identity.**

summaries.summary: 没人愿意退回全凭直觉与暗箱操作的纯主观世界——缺乏可验证的数据，弱者更容易在结构性偏见中沦为代价。众人的交集在于，**指标的失效并非道德崩塌，而是复杂系统遭遇外部干预时的必然位移**。真正的分歧在于药方：实证派主张通过拆分维度、公开数据与限制单维激励来修复标尺；自由演化与工程实践者则主张剥离中心化的奖惩特权，让度量退回为纯粹的探索信号；而批判与内省视角则警醒我们，无论指标如何优化，必须遏制其对个体价值认同与生存权力的全面吞噬。
summaries.insight: 在现代计算与复杂系统理论中，这种异化被称为“奖励作弊（Reward Hacking）”：**一旦在一个高维复杂世界上施加单一低维目标的强优化压力，代理指标与真实价值之间的裂隙就必然被无限放大。** 这是一条信息论上的数学铁律，而非管理不力或品格问题。许多人常误以为精细化等于科学化，但当一个系统的参数被穷尽度量时，该系统也就丧失了演化冗余。对于真实组织与个体而言，最重要的防护网是引入“对抗性指标（Counter-metrics）”：考核交付速度时，必须由一个完全独立的质量或退弹指标来掣肘，用不相容的张力锁住系统的变形空间。
summaries.advice: 本周你可以立即执行三件事：第一，应用“配对指标法”，**为你最核心的 KPI 配上一把反向制衡的尺子**（如追求工单数量时强制绑定客诉率，追求阅读书目时强制绑定笔记内化率），用双向张力避免大脑滑向捷径；第二，采纳阿马蒂亚·森的建议，面对当前最困扰你的一项考核，向评估方明确询问数据来源与申诉流程，将隐性标准显性化；第三，践行福柯的提议，本周留出不可被量化、不写进任何汇报的 90 分钟，只为真正重要的隐性价值工作。
summaries.summary_en: No one in the debate advocates returning to an opaque world governed purely by subjective intuition; without verifiable metrics, the vulnerable become collateral damage to hidden bias and noise. The core consensus is that **metric decay is not a moral failure, but a mathematical displacement when a complex system faces external pressure.** The divergence lies in the remedy: empirical thinkers argue for recalibrating metrics through dimensionality deconstruction and public auditing; practitioners and market theorists insist on stripping centralized reward-and-punishment hooks; while philosophical critics caution against allowing any yardstick to colonize personal identity and administrative power.
summaries.insight_en: Modern computational theory defines this divergence as reward hacking: **whenever intense optimization pressure is exerted on a low-dimensional proxy within a high-dimensional reality, the divergence between the proxy and true value exponentially widens.** This is an information-theoretic certainty rather than a managerial defect. Organizations mistakenly equate granular quantification with rigor, yet over-specified systems inevitably deplete their own adaptive slack. The pragmatic remedy is introducing counter-metrics: whenever an efficiency proxy is tracked, tether it to an orthogonal friction metric (such as defect rates or technical debt), creating generative tension that prevents the system from collapsing into shallow gaming.
summaries.advice_en: Take three concrete steps this week: First, adopt paired metrics: **pair your primary quantifiable goal with a counter-balancing metric** (e.g., balance output speed with rework frequency, or weight loss with energy levels) to prevent your dopamine circuitry from taking destructive shortcuts. Second, borrow Amartya Sen’s approach by actively inquiring about the raw data sources and formal appeal procedures of an evaluation metric currently applied to you. Finally, execute Foucault’s exercise: carve out 90 minutes this week for high-leverage work that will never appear on any KPI dashboard or review.

hooks.text: **不作为不入账**：改一件事要立项、签字、有人背责任；维持现状不用。于是拖延被记成稳健，而它的账单——机会关掉、最好的人走了——不出现在任何一张报表上。一份只记『做了什么』的账，该怎么补上『没做什么』这一栏？
hooks.text_en: **Inaction is never booked**: changing something takes a proposal, a signature and someone to carry it; leaving things alone takes none. So delay gets recorded as prudence, while its bill — the opportunity closed, the best people gone — appears on no report at all. How would a ledger that records only what was done add a column for what was not?

hooks.text: **测量与处置该不该共用一个时钟**：日报表今天出来，明天就连上奖金、排班与淘汰——既来不及验证这个数能不能预测真实结果，也分不清是业务变了还是人变了。高频只做诊断、低频才做处置，这条界线该由谁来守？
hooks.text_en: **Should measurement and consequence share one clock?** A dashboard number appears today and by tomorrow it is wired to bonuses, rosters and dismissals — too fast to test whether the number predicts the real outcome, and too fast to tell a change in the business from a change in behaviour. Diagnose at high frequency, decide about people at low frequency: who is supposed to hold that line?

hooks.text: **不可测之物的治理**：钱能被征税，因为钱看得见。尊荣、态度、观感没有计量单位，于是既不进考核，也不进再分配。可测的被考核坏，不可测的干脆逃出治理——这两件事其实是同一枚硬币的两面。
hooks.text_en: **Governing what cannot be measured**: money can be taxed because money is visible. Standing, bearing and the impression one makes have no unit of account, so they enter neither appraisal nor redistribution. What can be measured is spoilt by being graded; what cannot escapes governance altogether — two faces of one coin.

hooks.text: **被量的人也在量你**：考核从来不是单向的。下属会反推上司在乎什么，据此决定说什么、藏什么。一套指标公布的那一刻，也公布了定尺者的价值观与软肋——这一层反向的读心，有没有可能被正大光明地设计进去？
hooks.text_en: **The measured are measuring you too**: appraisal is never one-directional. Subordinates reverse-engineer what the boss cares about and decide accordingly what to say and what to hide. The moment a set of measures is published, so are the values and the soft spots of whoever set them. Could that reverse reading be designed in openly instead?

hooks.text: **谁有资格看到自己的原始分**：申诉权几乎决定了一套评价是治理工具还是处置工具，而多数机构的默认是只给结论、不给过程。这一层的沉默，往往比指标本身更能说明它想干什么。
hooks.text_en: **Who may see their own raw scores**: the right of appeal all but decides whether an appraisal is an instrument of governance or of disposal, and most institutions default to giving the verdict without the working. That silence usually says more about the system's intent than the measure itself does.
